title: Trace-distance-based complementarity relations in a multipath interferometer
authors: Yue Sun, Jingyan Liu, Peng-Tong Li, Chenxu Li, Ming-Jing Zhao
abstract: The complementarity relations in an interferometer reflect an important phenomenon in quantum mechanics: wave-particle duality. Here, we develop a method to quantify both wave and particle behaviors in a multi-path interferometer. In particular, we find that the trace distance is a good candidate for wave and particle measures. As a result, some duality relations and triality ralations are established respectively. This work not only extends the application of the trace distance to the interferometer, but also opens up new perspectives on the quantification of waveness and particleness.
summary: This paper introduces the use of the trace distance to quantify wave and particle aspects in multi-path interferometers, thereby establishing quantitative complementarity relations. It derives several upper bounds for the wave-particle duality and extends this analysis to include mixedness, providing a comprehensive theoretical framework for understanding quantum duality.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a rigorous method to quantify wave and particle behaviors in a multi-path interferometer and establish the resulting complementarity relations.
main_result: The trace distance proves to be a suitable measure for quantifying both wave and particle features, leading to the establishment of wave-particle dualities and trialities.
method: The authors utilize the trace distance, $T(ho, \sigma)$, as a general function $D$ to define quantitative measures for waveness ($W(ho)$) and particleness ($P(ho)$).
model_or_system: The study is based on the theoretical model of a $d$-path interferometer, where quantum states $ho$ are analyzed in the path basis $\{|iangle\}_d$.
key_observables: Waveness measure ($W_{tr}(ho)$), Particle measure ($P_{tr}(ho)$), Mixedness measures ($M(ho), M_1(ho), M_2(ho)$), and the trace distance $T(ho, \sigma)$.
important_parameters: The dimension of the interferometer ($d$), and the mixing parameter ($\epsilon$) when analyzing mixed states.
main_assumptions: The analysis sometimes assumes the state $ho$ is pure to simplify proofs, and the authors note that the trace distance is not necessarily a metric.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the interferometer and compare the derived upper bounds for the wave-particle duality ($W_{tr}^2 + P_{tr}^2$) against the exact value across various dimensions and mixing parameters.
paper_structure: The paper develops the general method using the trace distance, establishes the definitions for $W(ho)$ and $P(ho)$ via theorems, and then systematically derives and compares multiple upper bounds for the duality and triality relations.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental mathematical tools (trace distance quantification) to analyze the core quantum mechanical concept of wave-particle duality in an interferometer setting, which has direct implications for quantum sensing and measurement theory.
